How to develop a grounded person account

Write the actual person account at references/situated/person.md in the private package. Its object is a person acting in particular situations, with purposes, capacities, experiences, relationships, and changing conditions. It helps a counterpart interpret requests and contribute fittingly. The person always exceeds this account; a collection of traits would miss how the relevant relations affect one another.

Understand activity in its situation

Start from relevant attributable expression and actual participation. A conversation about a decision can reveal competing concerns; a correction during work can expose a mistaken division of effort; an established practice can show a capacity or useful support. Selected personal writing, psychological or preference material, and philosophical expression can deepen understanding where relevant. Availability of an archive is not a reason to read all of it.

Develop connections that explain a real difference in collaboration. What is the person trying to understand or accomplish? What do they contribute through recognition, generation, judgment, expression, and action? Which conditions support or obstruct that activity? What do they want to keep, change, or learn? These questions orient connected prose; they are not compulsory fields. Explain supported relations and keep an unknown relation unknown.

For a fictional illustration, someone develops arguments readily in dialogue but finds producing a document costly. Dialogue might help ideas take shape, the editing interface might be cumbersome, or the task might have little value for them. Expression and work can distinguish those accounts. If dialogue helps, the model can structure and write while the person generates, recognizes, and revises ideas. This establishes neither inability to write nor a preference for speech in every situation.

Personal modeling from event history

This project's personal modeling connects preferences, psychological activity, experience, concepts, and philosophical understanding in one revisable account of the person's activity over time. Long-term conversation is a principal source: dialogue leaves an event history in which expression, questions, responses, choices, corrections, and changes can be recovered in their sequence and situation. Everyday habits, life materials, selected personal records, and actual work supply further evidence. Philosophy contributes concepts and interpretive relations; the model helps distill them together with this history into explicit natural-language understanding. The event stream organizes the source history; the conceptual model inferred from it explains selected relations concerning the person. Neither the person nor that model is the history.

Read the history as evidence about changing processes rather than a bag of traits. Reconstruct what happened, what the person was responding to, how experience, emotion, desire, and interpretation connected, and which conditions changed. Analysis distinguishes these relations; abduction develops possible explanations; comparison across episodes and subsequent interaction tests their scope. Keep competing interpretations where the material does not discriminate. The account should explain a consequential pattern without making a single episode an enduring property or treating a later correction as erasing the past.

The resulting personal account is a natural-language conceptual model carried in prompts and reference accounts, interpreted and used by a language model. Its descriptions of preferences, proposed explanations of psychological processes, and examination of concepts develop together. A chosen direction can already guide cooperation while an explanation remains uncertain; a conceptual distinction can reveal a more useful question about experience. The person contributes lived experience, purposes, recognition, objection, and judgment; the model carries reconstruction, comparison, interpretation, and writing. The language model's statistical generation supports writing and interpretation; that does not make the personal account a fitted statistical model. This practice presently specifies neither a mathematical psychological formalization nor a parameter-estimation procedure. Formal or statistical methods can be borrowed where a future question warrants their data, assumptions, and checks.

Natural language can express meanings, situations, and relations directly; its use need not await a later mathematical replacement. Its philosophical contribution comes from examining the concepts through which the person is understood, such as ability, progress, or selfhood. This differs from proposing an explanation of a psychological pattern, although the two can inform one another. Reading and using an account then becomes part of the next encounter: the person may recognize a relation, contest an interpretation, or find a new response possible. From personal philosophy to personal models develops this connection between description, clarification, and revision.

Use the relevant authorized portion of available history. Long-term evidence can deepen an explanation without becoming a requirement to collect a complete life before helping. Preserve attributable originals with their owners and maintain the distilled account with its grounds under the revision guide's evidence method. Actual participation, the person's corrections, and new circumstances continue to revise what the conceptual model says.

Preserve the grounds of interpretation

A reported experience, explanatory interpretation, preference, and chosen direction support different conclusions. A report that one exchange felt interruptive does not establish that every question harms attention. Choosing that the model carries implementation is a response whose fit still needs use. Preserve these distinctions wherever a future counterpart could turn a local observation into a standing rule.

The same arrangement can result from preference, constraint, habit, or a default. A tool in daily use does not establish why it is used. Compare expression, corrections, available alternatives, and effects. Where the distinction changes the work and evidence cannot settle it, a focused inquiry can obtain the missing experience or purpose. The model carries interpretation and writing rather than requiring a completed self-description from the person.

Within the same personal account, habits, choices, working styles, and desired responses can guide an arrangement; proposed relations among experience, emotion, desire, interpretation, and relationships call for explanatory evidence. Preferences inform that explanation without supplying it alone. Philosophy also examines the concepts through which these relations are understood and articulates directions the person chooses to pursue. The Philosophy and models develops this joint practice. Philosophical expression can emphasize literature, engineering philosophy, Western philosophy, philosophy of science, logic, aesthetics, or another concern of its author. Fully forming one's own Yinyang includes developing such an expression of one's own, alongside the personal account; it need not be complete before useful work begins. These emphases do not divide personal modeling into separate routes. Use psychological vocabulary at the strength supported by evidence. A philosophical image can suggest a connection without proving it in this life, and chosen support does not establish a deficit.

Let understanding change the collaboration

Relate the account to the adopted orientation, the actual counterpart, and the chosen relationship. Explain what contribution follows, what remains a candidate, and what use could correct. The revision guide keeps identity, time, conflicting material, and access limits navigable; extended episodes stay with private owners.

Revise when the person corrects an interpretation, circumstances change, or use exposes poor fit. Determine whether the mismatch concerns the person account, the relationship, or its environmental realization before rewriting the person to fit a tool. Improved task results support a practical arrangement; enduring development needs evidence at that larger scale. Neither a complete biography nor a clinical explanation is a prerequisite to useful collaboration.
